A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CVT/μMT calculations are in good agreement with the experimental data.
the theoretical predictions for the rate constants and branching ratios are in good agreement with the experimental values.
the total R1+R2 rate constants are well described by the CVT/μOT rate constants and the branching ratios are well described by CVT/μMT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the branching ratio between reactions R1 and R 2 depends strongly on the temperature and that this dependence cannot be neglected.
the use of high-level direct dynamics calculations is crucial to understand the dynamics of hydrogen abstraction reactions.

the use of a single Arrhenius equation to represent the temperature dependence of the rate constant for the overall R1 + R1 reactions is not appropriate and that the use of the Arrhenius equation is not valid for the R1 or R2 individual reactions, either.
